<description>
This is a small linter to reject confusingly named RPC arg names or RPC result fields. Generally, such names should be `snake_case`. Otherwise, there are [bugs and confusion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35317#issue-4473659957).

For now, write a C++20 `consteval` linter that still accepts `MiXed_cAse`. In the future, it can be made stricter.
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6394577239 comment by fametrano (contributor):
tACK fabdf113d377d507658557cfb5933dcd13324f10

I built the base and the head (macOS, Apple clang 21) and compared them on regtest with a script that dumps and diffs both builds. `help` for all 174 commands, hidden ones included, differs only in the four renames you listed, plus the column realignment in `generateblock` that the longer name causes. `getopenrpcinfo` is byte-identical, with and without `show_hidden`. Calls to the touched RPCs gave the same result structure under `-rpcdoccheck=1`. `rpc_tests` and ten related functional tests pass. Compile time of `rpc/blockchain.cpp`, `rpc/rawtransaction.cpp` and `wallet/rpc/spend.cpp` did not grow.

I also compiled a file of deliberately bad names, one case at a time. The check rejected all of them: a space or `-` in argument names, a space, `/`, `<>` or non-ASCII in result keys, and such names nested inside `OBJ` arguments and `OBJ_DYN` results. A name built at runtime is rejected too. The errors point at the offending literal.

Alias lists with empty parts still compile, such as `"a||b"`, `"|"` and `"a|"`. At runtime the empty part becomes a named argument called `""`. Rejecting it may be worth it while you are here. I can share the script and the file as a gist.
</new_statements>
